name: MMI Real-Time Server Monitor
excerpt: Live server health for WordPress: load, CPU, memory and visitors at a glance, with likely bad visitors flagged.
intro: MMI Real-Time Server Monitor shows what your server is doing right now from inside WordPress: load, CPU, memory, PHP workers and visitors in the last minute. It also points out visitors who look like trouble, so you can see a problem building before your store slows down.

features.text: Live dashboard, with a history of high-load incidents
Logs every load alert, and emails you when WordPress's scheduled jobs back up
Visitors in the last minute, counted from your web server's log or from the pages WordPress serves
Flags likely bad visitors: probing for weak spots, repeated login attempts, fake Google or Bing crawlers
Copy their addresses, or a ready-made Cloudflare rule to block them
Works on dedicated, VPS and shared hosting (shows what each host exposes)

screenshots.title: Auto-remediation
screenshots.caption: Optionally take the site offline for visitors while load is critical.
features: Off by default; when on, the site goes into maintenance mode at Critical and Emergency load, for non-admin visitors only, until load recovers
Grace periods: Critical needs 3 checks over 120 seconds, Emergency 2 checks over 60 seconds
Logging, alerts and the rtsm_critical_load / rtsm_emergency_mode_* hooks run whether it is on or off
System information for support requests
